newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah little changed in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah little changed in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah was little changed against the dollar in slow Monday trade, dealers said.
They said overnight comments by finance minister Mar'ie Muhammad in Washington seemed to remain the market focus.
Mar'ie said that his country would rather have its rupiah undervalued than overvalued and added Indonesia intended to depreciate the currency by five percent per year against the U.S. dollar.
One U.S. bank dealer said the statement was a reiteration of previously stated targets although the rupiah fell initially.
"There was nothing new. Offshore operators were pushing the dollar up in early morning but failed to break through on lack of momentum," the dealer said.

He said the dollar was well offered at the 2,325.00 level. Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,321.7/22.7 at 0850 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,319.25/20.00. It fell to a low of 2,324.5 in early Singapore trading.
Dealers said trading was slow after the short-lived reaction to the minister's statement, mainly from offshore operators.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,321.25/21.75 and 2,320.00/21.00, respectively.
